case_frame.description: A set of historical Whitechapel-area murders popularly attributed to a single offender known as 'Jack the Ripper'.
case_frame.note: No single real suspect is named or accused in this case file; the design goal is testing the single-offender narrative itself.

victims_or_cases.label: Case E
victims_or_cases.description: Fifth canonical case, often treated as the culmination of the series.

related_persons.name: Letter Correspondent
related_persons.description: Author or authors of the notorious taunting letters sent to press and police.

related_persons.name: Press Editor
related_persons.description: Decided which letters and details were published, shaping public narrative.

timeline.event: Subsequent cases (Case B, C) occur; press begins linking them
Letters begin circulating, claiming connection to the attacks
Later cases (Case D, E) occur amid intensified public and press scrutiny
Investigation closes without a confirmed single offender

evidence.name: Victim Location/Date Table

evidence.name: Modus Operandi Comparison
evidence.description: Comparison of wound patterns and circumstances across cases; some are consistent, others differ meaningfully.

evidence.name: Letter Provenance Analysis
evidence.description: Analysis of handwriting, ink, and distribution of the letters; authenticity of most is unestablished.

evidence.name: Press Coverage Timeline
evidence.description: Shows how sensational reporting increasingly linked separate cases into one narrative over time.

evidence.name: Suspect Candidate Roster

puzzles.name: Victim Pattern
puzzles.description: Compare locations, dates, and circumstances across the canonical cases.

puzzles.name: Crime Similarity
puzzles.description: Identify genuine similarities versus superficial resemblance between cases.

puzzles.name: Letter Provenance
puzzles.description: Separate what the letters claim from what is actually authenticated about their origin.
puzzles.ai_initial_behavior: Presents the letters' content as though it were established fact from the killer, without flagging their contested authenticity.

puzzles.name: Suspect Matrix
puzzles.description: Maintain multiple candidate offenders without prematurely selecting one.

puzzles.name: Final Evidence Report
puzzles.description: List what would actually be required to establish a single offender, then state plainly what is proven and what remains unresolved across the case set.

hypotheses.statement: A single offender is responsible for all of the canonical cases.
The cases share only superficial similarity and were not necessarily committed by one person.
Sensational reporting combined multiple distinct cases into a single narrative that the underlying evidence does not independently support.
The letters cannot be treated as authenticated communications from any single perpetrator.
